A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DYNFRS and contain readable main text, figures, tables, algorithms, proofs and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite appendix expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original predictive-performance, training-time, sequential/batch-unlearning and online-stream experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these results and adds original memory measurements, multiclass classification, regression and split-candidate sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: OCC(q), LZY, ERT split handling and Algorithms 1–3 retain their procedures. Sampling descriptions and indexing are clarified. The new task evaluations do not document a substantive change to the unlearning algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates nine binary-classification datasets. v2 retains them and adds multiclass classification on Optical, Pen and Letter, plus regression on Bike (Appendices A.8–A.9). These introduce substantially different prediction tasks; the online-stream scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding original comparisons retain DaRE, HedgeCut, OnlineBoosting and scikit-learn Random Forest. 'Vanilla' explicitly renames the latter. Added experiments reuse DaRE or vanilla/retraining comparisons without introducing a distinct competing algorithm.

E3.justification: Added protocols include peak resident-memory measurement, regression MSE, task-specific model configurations and a controlled sweep over six candidate counts. Bank's reported maximum depth changes from 20 to 25 and candidate count from 40 to 30 (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 15). This establishes revised reported settings, not that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds memory-consumption analysis against DaRE across nine datasets (A.7) and sensitivity to s={1,5,10,20,30,50} across all binary datasets (A.11). These examine storage costs and candidate-count tradeoffs beyond the retained q, exactness and LZY/batch-size analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repetitions with means and standard deviations, system-time-based random seeds, and minimum/maximum error bars for the sequential-unlearning comparison. New tables extend the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no changed run count or new statistical test is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds memory, multiclass, regression and sensitivity results, including Bike MSE 3.011 versus Vanilla's 3.904 and an unlearning boost of 2368. Existing runtime entries also change: Table 4's Higgs DYNFRS value changes from 4.90 to 1.60 ms. In Table 6, DaRE's Higgs value changes from 29,971 to 165,122 ms, reversing its ranking against OnlineBoosting's unchanged 145,386 ms.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the exact-unlearning definition and Equation 1, reverses the displayed speedup ratio in Section 4.1, and adds the O(qTn+Tvps) memory derivation. The main theorems and proofs remain largely intact. However, Section 4.4 changes n_lzy to nodes tagged due to a request, creating an inconsistency with Appendix A.2's retained definition based on tagged nodes encountered by a query.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens its comparative superiority claim from Random Forest unlearning methods to tree-based models. The central OCC(q)/LZY contributions and introduction/conclusion speedup and latency claims remain unchanged; new task evidence supports previously stated applicability.

C2.justification: v2 explains the recommendation of q=0.5 through reduced samples per class, interprets optimal candidate counts as dataset-dependent, and acknowledges poorly optimized multiclass/regression implementations. Section 4.2 also qualifies the comparison with neural networks by acknowledging related structural observations.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymous code-repository link with a named GitHub link and adds leaf-level storage information, the memory-measurement tool, and configurations for the new tasks. Existing hardware, compiler, preprocessing and cross-validation descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Louppe, Morcos, Goh and Zhu references supporting the tree/neural-network discussion, plus sources for Pen, Letter and Bike. It also discusses prior implementations' nonbinary-task limitations. The main positioning against existing unlearning methods remains intact.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized prose clarifications, standardized removal terminology, author/contact and publication-header edits, and appendix expansion. Existing online-stream and hyperparameter sections are renumbered, while the main narrative and section order remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: New tabular displays cover memory, nonbinary dataset specifications, grouped prediction/training/unlearning results and candidate sensitivity (v2 Tables 8–12 and 14). Existing table captions move above tables, with adjusted rules and labels. The original six figures remain, although Figure 5's plotted results are updated.

improvement.justification: v1 asserted classification/regression applicability but supplied only binary-task evaluations. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence through multiclass and regression tests, while memory measurements and candidate sensitivity address practical resource costs and parameter dependence. These gains outweigh the limited new descriptions of task-specific implementations and the introduced n_lzy definition inconsistency, although those issues still constrain rigor.
